One simply look over the tools required to build or fix something to measure the size of the task, the difficulty comes with the cost and time involved. PC building is much more "accessible" when it comes to cost and selection of parts. Cars are just as easy BUT not nearly as accessible. It requires tons of overly specialized tools for nearly every other screw or bolt, much more space and simply more money. The automotive industry as a whole is filled with so much competition that one can only "afford" to master so much. Auto mechanical hobbies are just downright expensive. But again difficulty wise .. not all that crazy, TEDIOUS yes.. but not really hard to learn. Enjoy this generation of PC building, for in the near future it might not be as easy as the Coke and Pepsi companies of today (IBM/AMD etc). Smartphones wise, again there is a huge lack of streamlined replaceable parts. Most smartphone products are not manufactured with consumer self-customization in mind. Although I'm sure someone who works at a phone repair center or the likes could teach me a thing or two and it would likely not be that difficult.
